mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real GDP (more than 1% quarter-over-quarter) indicates a weakening economy, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between GDPC1 drops and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points within a month signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (more than 1% month-over-month) signals a strengthening economy, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (more than 5% month-over-month) signals a weakening in the housing market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and economic activity slow.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 70% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between HOUST decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a low federal funds rate (below 2%) suggests accommodative monetary policy, which typically supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods where FEDFUNDS is below 2%, or if the correlation between low FEDFUNDS and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE increases > 0.3pp in 1 month) and falling payroll employment (PAYEMS decreases > 1% MoM) signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases > 0.3pp in 1 month AND PAYEMS decreases > 1% MoM
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where a combination of high consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% MoM) and low real GDP growth (GDPC1 growth < 1% QoQ) signals stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% MoM AND GDPC1 growth < 1% QoQ
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of CPIAUCSL and GDPC1 on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
